notes.title: Design System Documentation
notes.content:
TechFlow Design System — v2.0
Last updated: 2026-02-25 | Owner: Derek Lam

## Foundations

Colors:
- Primary: #2563EB (Blue 600)
- Secondary: #7C3AED (Purple 600)
- Success: #059669 (Green 600)
- Warning: #D97706 (Amber 600)
- Error: #DC2626 (Red 600)
- Neutral: Gray scale (50-950)

Typography:
- Display: Inter, 48/56px, -0.02em tracking
- Heading 1: Inter, 32/40px, -0.01em
- Heading 2: Inter, 24/32px
- Body: Inter, 16/24px
- Caption: Inter, 12/16px
- Code: JetBrains Mono, 14/20px

Spacing: 4px base unit (4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96)

Border radius:
- Small: 4px (buttons, inputs)
- Medium: 8px (cards, panels)
- Large: 16px (modals, popovers)
- Full: 9999px (pills, avatars)

## Components
- Button (primary, secondary, ghost, destructive) — 3 sizes
- Input (text, search, select, textarea)
- Card (default, interactive, elevated)
- Modal (small, medium, large)
- Toast (info, success, warning, error)
- Sidebar (collapsed, expanded)
- Context Panel (the core AI feature component)

## Patterns
- Loading states: skeleton screens (never spinners)
- Empty states: illustration + CTA
- Error states: inline message + retry action
- Responsive breakpoints: 640, 768, 1024, 1280, 1536px

notes.title: Project Alpha UI Specifications
notes.content:
Project Alpha — UI Specification Document
Version: 2.1 | Last updated: 2026-02-20

## Context Panel (Core Feature)
Position: Right sidebar, 320px width (collapsible)
Trigger: Auto-opens based on user focus; manual toggle via keyboard shortcut (Cmd+Shift+K)

Layout:
- Header: 'Relevant Context' + source indicator + collapse button
- Content area: scrollable list of context cards
- Each card: title, snippet, source icon, relevance score (hidden), timestamp
- Footer: 'Show more' link + feedback buttons (helpful/not helpful)

Context Card Variants:
1. Document card: title, preview text, last editor, source app
2. Message card: sender avatar, message excerpt, channel/DM name
3. Meeting card: meeting title, attendees, date, key points
4. Task card: task title, status, assignee, project

## Search Interface
Position: Center of screen, full-width modal (Cmd+K trigger)
Layout:
- Input: large search field with placeholder 'Search across all your tools...'
- Filters row: tool icons + date range + type filter
- Results: grouped by tool, ranked by relevance
- Right panel: preview of selected result

## Animations
- Context panel slide-in: 200ms ease-out
- Card entrance: stagger 50ms, fade+slide up
- Search modal: scale from 0.95 + fade, 150ms
- Loading: pulse animation on skeleton cards

## Accessibility
- All interactive elements keyboard navigable
- Screen reader announcements for context updates
- Focus management in modal states
- Minimum contrast ratio: 4.5:1 (WCAG AA)
- Reduced motion: respect prefers-reduced-motion

notes.title: Accessibility Audit Report
notes.content:
Accessibility Audit Report — TechFlow AI Desktop App
Date: 2026-02-22 | Auditor: Derek Lam
Standard: WCAG 2.1 Level AA

## Summary
Total issues found: 18
- Critical (A violations): 7
- Major (AA violations): 6
- Minor (best practices): 5

## Critical Issues (must fix before launch)

1. [CRIT-01] Context panel cards not keyboard accessible
   - Arrow keys don't navigate between cards
   - No visible focus indicator on cards
   - Fix: Add tabindex, focus styles, arrow key navigation

2. [CRIT-02] Search modal traps focus incorrectly
   - Tab cycles through modal but Escape doesn't close
   - Background content still interactive
   - Fix: Proper focus trap with Escape handler

3. [CRIT-03] Color contrast failures in secondary text
   - Gray 400 on white = 3.0:1 (needs 4.5:1)
   - Affects: timestamps, meta text, placeholders
   - Fix: Use Gray 600 minimum for all text

4. [CRIT-04] No alt text on tool integration icons
   - Screen readers announce 'image' instead of 'Slack', 'Notion', etc.
   - Fix: Add descriptive alt attributes

5. [CRIT-05] Form inputs missing labels
   - Search input, filter dropdowns have no associated labels
   - Fix: Add aria-label or visible labels

6. [CRIT-06] Live region not announcing context updates
   - When new context cards appear, screen readers don't announce
   - Fix: aria-live='polite' on context panel container

7. [CRIT-07] Toast notifications disappear without notice
   - Auto-dismiss toasts not announced to screen readers
   - Fix: role='alert' + aria-live='assertive'

## Estimated Fix Effort
- Critical fixes: 5 engineering days (Lisa volunteered)
- Major fixes: 3 engineering days
- Total: 8 days if parallelized

## Recommendation
Fix all critical issues before March 15 launch. Major issues can be addressed in v1.1.

notes.content:
User Flow Diagrams — Key Flows (Summary)

Flow 1: New User Onboarding (2-step)
Landing Page → Sign Up (email/Google) → Connect First Tool → Success State → Home Feed
                                                                  ↓
                                                          (if skip) → Home Feed (empty state with nudge)

Flow 2: Cross-Tool Search
Anywhere → Cmd+K → Type Query → See Results (grouped by tool) → Click Result → View in Source App
                                          ↓
                                   (if no results) → Suggest broader search or different tool

Flow 3: Context Panel Interaction
User Working → AI Detects Context → Panel Slides In → User Scans Cards → Clicks Card → Opens Source
                                                              ↓
                                                    (if not helpful) → Dismiss + Feedback

Flow 4: Meeting Prep
Calendar Event Approaching → Notification → Open TechFlow → Meeting Context Card → Related Docs + Attendee Info → Join Meeting

Flow 5: Enterprise Admin
Admin Login → Admin Dashboard → View Users → Manage Permissions → View Analytics → Export Report

notes.title: Animation Guidelines
notes.content:
TechFlow Animation Guidelines

Principles:
1. Purposeful: Every animation must serve a function (orient, guide, or delight)
2. Swift: Most transitions under 300ms. Users should never wait for animations.
3. Natural: Use ease-out for entrances, ease-in for exits. Spring physics for interactive.
4. Accessible: Always respect prefers-reduced-motion. Provide static alternatives.

Duration Scale:
- Micro (50-100ms): button state changes, icon transitions
- Fast (150-200ms): tooltips, dropdowns, small reveals
- Medium (200-300ms): modal open/close, panel slide, page transitions
- Slow (300-500ms): complex orchestrated sequences, onboarding

Easing:
- Entrance: cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.2, 1) — ease-out
- Exit: cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 1, 1) — ease-in
- Interaction: cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1) — ease-in-out
- Spring: tension 200, friction 20 (for drag/swipe)

Specific Animations:
- Context Panel: translateX(320px) → translateX(0), 200ms ease-out
- Search Modal: scale(0.95) + opacity(0) → scale(1) + opacity(1), 150ms
- Card stagger: opacity(0) + translateY(8px) → visible, 50ms delay between cards
- Toast: translateY(-100%) → translateY(0), 200ms ease-out, auto-dismiss after 5s with fadeOut

Implementation:
- Use CSS transitions for simple state changes
- Use Framer Motion for complex orchestration
- Never use requestAnimationFrame for UI animations (use CSS/library)

notes.title: Design Sprint Output — Notification System
notes.content:
Design Sprint: Notification System Redesign
Duration: 3 days (Feb 12-14, 2026)
Participants: Derek, Tina, Lisa

Problem: Users get overwhelmed by notifications from connected tools. Current design shows everything in a flat list.

Solution: AI-Grouped Notifications

Concept:
- Group notifications by context (project, meeting, person) not by tool
- AI determines priority: urgent (red dot), important (blue dot), FYI (no dot)
- Digest mode: collect non-urgent items and show summary at set times

UI Design:
- Notification panel: right sidebar (same area as context panel — tabs)
- Groups: collapsible sections with summary header
  e.g., 'Project Alpha — 4 new items' → expand to see individual items
- Quick actions: reply, snooze, mark as read without opening source app
- Settings: per-tool and per-group notification preferences

Prototype tested with 5 users:
- 4/5 preferred grouped over flat list
- 3/5 found AI priority accurate
- Feedback: want to customize groups + override AI priority

Next steps:
- Tina to add to Q2 roadmap
- Engineering estimate needed from Mike
- Revisit after mobile launch

notes.title: User Testing Session Notes
notes.content:
User Testing — Mobile Prototype (5 participants)
Date: 2026-02-26
Facilitator: Derek | Observer: Tina

Participants: 5 beta users (mix of PM, engineer, designer)

Task 1: Find a Slack message from last week about 'budget'
- 4/5 found it within 20 seconds using search
- 1/5 tried scrolling the home feed (expected to see it there)
- Voice search: 3/5 tried it, all successful

Task 2: Prepare for a meeting in 30 minutes
- 5/5 went to Meetings tab
- 4/5 understood the context card layout
- 1/5 confused by 'related documents' section (expected links not previews)

Task 3: Save a link for later
- 3/5 found Quick Capture immediately
- 2/5 looked for a 'save' button in the home feed
- Insight: need a 'save' action on cards, not just in Capture tab

Task 4: Dismiss a non-relevant notification
- 5/5 discovered swipe-to-dismiss
- 3/5 wanted to 'mute' that type of notification (not just dismiss)
- Add: long-press → 'mute notifications from this source'

Key Insights:
- Navigation is intuitive (bottom tabs well-understood)
- Voice search is popular (surprised me — 60% usage)
- Cards need clearer actions (save, share, mute)
- Meeting prep is the killer feature for mobile

Design changes:
- Add save/share/mute actions on long-press menu
- Make voice button larger (users love it)
- Add 'related docs' explainer text on first use

notes.title: Brand Workshop Notes
notes.content:
Brand Workshop — Visual Identity Refresh
Date: 2026-02-15
Attendees: Derek, Nina, Sarah
Facilitator: Nina

Objective: Align on visual identity for public launch

Current brand: Functional, clean, but generic. Looks like every other SaaS tool.
Desired brand: Approachable AI. Smart but not intimidating. Trustworthy.

Mood board themes:
1. 'Calm Technology' — muted colors, lots of whitespace, subtle gradients
2. 'Playful Intelligence' — rounded shapes, illustrations, micro-animations
3. 'Premium Simplicity' — minimal, high-contrast, bold typography

Group decision: Hybrid of 1 + 2
- Calm overall aesthetic (white space, muted palette)
- Playful moments in illustrations and animations (personality)
- Premium typography (Inter is good, but upgrade marketing font to Outfit)

Logo discussion:
- Current logo works but feels too 'techy'
- Adding a subtle sparkle/glow to the icon (AI signal)
- No full rebrand now — minor refresh for launch

Marketing vs. Product:
- Marketing site: more expressive (illustrations, larger type, gradients)
- Product UI: more restrained (functional, information-dense)
- Both share same color palette and typography
